service.description: Always returns the latest 100 articles for any `topic`, `country`, `lang`, or any of those combined

optional_parameters.description:
Specifies the language of the search.  Allowed values are:
`af`, `ar`, `bg`, `bn`, `ca`,`cn`, `cs`, `cy`, `da`, `de`, `el`, `en`, `es`, `et`, `fa`, `fi`, `fr`, `gu`, `he`, `hi`, `hr`, `hu`, `id`, `it`, `ja`, `kn`, `ko`, `lt`, `lv`, `mk`, `ml`, `mr`, `ne`, `nl`, `no`, `pa`, `pl`, `pt`, `ro`, `ru`, `sk`, `sl`, `so`, `sq`, `sv`, `sw`, `ta`, `te`, `th`, `tl`, `tr`,`tw`, `uk`, `ur`, `vi`. 
 Specifying the language will make your search more relevant
optional_parameters.name: lang

optional_parameters.description:
The topic to which you want to restrict the articles of your choice. This parameter is [experimental]. Accepted values are `news`, `sport`, `tech`, `world`, `finance`, `politics`, `business`, `economics`, `entertainment`,`beauty`,`travel`,`music`,`food`,`science`
- `news` usually means a general news feed (main headlines of a website).
> Important: this parameter is [experimental]. Not all news articles are assigned with a `topic`, therefore, we cannot guarantee that 100% of topics talking about technology will be assigned a `tech` label.
> One topic at a time, for example `topic=sport`
optional_parameters.name: topic

optional_parameters.description: The country to which you want to narrow your search. This parameter is [experimental]. We advise you to use it in conjunction with the `lang` parameter. Accepts any [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) codes
optional_parameters.name: country

optional_parameters.description:
Adds to the output of the call two more variables: `media` and `media_content`

Media - the main image published with an article 

media_content  - a comma-separated string of all images used in an article
optional_parameters.name: media

service.description:
Almost all news domains including major outlets such as New York Times publish lots of articles that are not hard news, but rather clickbaits. 

Use our smart labels to identify and filter out such news articles by using headline and meta_description text as input.

The labels are below:

Non-News: This category includes articles that are often referred to as "soft news." Unlike traditional news articles that report on a specific event or breaking news, non-news articles focus on evergreen topics that are not time-sensitive. Examples of non-news articles include how-to guides, tips, reviews, and general profiles. These articles may be more feature-like in nature, and can often be enjoyed by readers at any time.

Opinion: This category includes articles that express a strong point of view, such as editorials, opinion pieces, letters to the editor, or other content that may be subjective in nature.

Paid News: This category includes articles that are sponsored or paid for by a brand or advertiser, often in the form of advertorials. The goal of these articles is typically to promote a product, service, or brand.

Pop Culture: This category covers articles related to entertainment and popular culture, such as stories about celebrities, movies, TV shows, music, fashion, and other trends.

Fact Check: This category includes articles that seek to verify the validity of rumors or questionable claims, with the goal of combating misinformation. Fact-checking articles typically provide evidence-based information and sources to support their claims.

Roundup: This category includes articles that summarize multiple stories or provide a collection of concepts, takeaways, data analysis, or lists. Roundup articles can be useful for readers who want to quickly get up-to-speed on a particular topic or trend.

Press Release: This category includes official statements or announcements, typically published by wire services and authored by organizations or PR professionals. Press releases may cover a variety of topics, such as new products, partnerships, or other news related to the organization.

News: This category includes traditional news articles that report on a specific event or breaking news. These articles are typically objective in nature and report on facts related to the event or news story.

service.description: Searches as `/v1/search` but returns the articles count per hour or day instead of articles' data

optional_parameters.description: The country to which you want to narrow your search. This parameter is [experimental]. We advise you to use it in conjunction with the `lang` parameter. Accepts any [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) codes
optional_parameters.name: country

optional_parameters.description:
The topic to which you want to restrict the articles of your choice. This parameter is [experimental]. Accepted values are `news`, `sport`, `tech`, `world`, `finance`, `politics`, `business`, `economics`, `entertainment`,`beauty`,`travel`,`music`,`food`,`science`
- `news` usually means a general news feed (main headlines of a website).
> Important: this parameter is [experimental]. Not all news articles are assigned with a `topic`, therefore, we cannot guarantee that 100% of topics talking about technology will be assigned a `tech` label.
> One topic at a time, for example, `topic=sport`
optional_parameters.name: topic

optional_parameters.description:
One or more news resources to filter your search. It should be the normal form of the URL, for example, **[nytimes.com](http://nytimes.com/)**, **[theguardian.com](http://theguardian.com/)**
> Comma separated string, for example `sources=nytimes.com,cnn.com,wsj.com`
optional_parameters.name: sources

optional_parameters.description:
- `day` — default option. Aggregate results by day. No more than 100 days 
- `hour` — Aggregate results by hour. No more than 100 hours
optional_parameters.name: agg_by

optional_parameters.description: Upper boundary of the rank of news website to filter by
optional_parameters.name: to_rank

optional_parameters.description:
Adds to the output of the call two more variables: `media` and `media_content`

Media - the main image published with an article 

media_content  - a comma-separated string of all images used in an article
optional_parameters.name: media

optional_parameters.description:
Specifies the language of the search.  Allowed values are:
`af`, `ar`, `bg`, `bn`, `ca`,`cn`, `cs`, `cy`, `da`, `de`, `el`, `en`, `es`, `et`, `fa`, `fi`, `fr`, `gu`, `he`, `hi`, `hr`, `hu`, `id`, `it`, `ja`, `kn`, `ko`, `lt`, `lv`, `mk`, `ml`, `mr`, `ne`, `nl`, `no`, `pa`, `pl`, `pt`, `ro`, `ru`, `sk`, `sl`, `so`, `sq`, `sv`, `sw`, `ta`, `te`, `th`, `tl`, `tr`,`tw`, `uk`, `ur`, `vi`. 
Specifying the language will make your search more relevant
optional_parameters.name: lang

optional_parameters.description:
One or more sources to be excluded from the search. 
> Comma separated string, for example, `not_sources=nytimes.com,cnn.com,wsj.com`
optional_parameters.name: not_sources

optional_parameters.description: Until which point in time to search for. The default timezone is UTC
optional_parameters.name: to

optional_parameters.description: Limit the search only for the sources which are in top 1 million online websites. Defaults to `True` (`False` if you want to turn it off). Unranked sources are assigned a rank that equals to `999999`
optional_parameters.name: ranked_only

optional_parameters.description:
From which point in time to start the search. No specific format is required. E.g. (`2020/05/01`, `2020-05-01` ,`2020-05-01 12:54:14`, `2020-05-01 4:15am`, `yesterday 2:02 am`, `2020/05/01 12:55 EST`) Default timezone is UTC. **
The default is set to one week ago at midnight UTC.**
optional_parameters.name: from

optional_parameters.description: By default, we search what you specified in `q` in both `title` and `summary` of the article. However, you can limit this to either `title` or `summary`
optional_parameters.name: search_in

optional_parameters.description: Lowest boundary of the rank of news website to filter by. **Important**: lower rank means that a source is more popular
optional_parameters.name: from_rank

required_parameters.description: String to search for. Has to be [URL-encoded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percent-encoding).
required_parameters.name: q
